answer: A sybil ring's tell is that its members never really disagree. So weight each peer endorsement by history: it counts in full only if, across the last 50 panels where the two IDs graded the same answers, their scores differed on at least 10% of them. A ring of clones that always agree reads like karst, solid on top but hollowed by hidden channels, and its mutual votes drop to zero. Faking disputes means scoring off consensus, which audits already punish, so clones lose their footing on that ledge either way. Honest critics keep basalt weight. The 50 and 10% are my guesses.
